methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. For the original research topic, the decomposition focused on the functional requirements related to the shift register enable signal and the reset signal. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition considered both the combinational logic and the timing logic aspects, extracting atomic units related to the behavior of the shift_ena signal under different conditions.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Module controls a shift register using an FSM.
Shift register should be enabled (shift_ena asserted) for exactly 4 clock cycles upon reset.
shift_ena is de-asserted and remains low until the next reset after the initial 4 cycles.
When a specific bit pattern is detected, shift_ena is asserted for 4 clock cycles.
Activation of the shift register is synchronous to the rising edge of the clock.
spec_atomic_units: Module has three ports: clk, reset, and shift_ena.
reset is an input synchronous active-high reset.
shift_ena is an output enable signal for a shift register.
shift_ena is asserted for 4 clock cycles upon reset.
Assertion and de-assertion of shift_ena are synchronous to the rising edge of clk.
The value of shift_ena at any given clock cycle depends on the history of the reset signal.
The module uses registers to track the number of clock cycles since the last reset.
The FSM has at least 5 states: reset, and 4 states to count the 4 clock cycles.
The clock edge is positive (rising edge).
